goal: Adds new C++ assert-style test macros (ASSERT, ASSERT_EQ, etc.) to replace Boost's BOOST_CHECK family.
Fixes correctness gaps in Boost's macros: signed/unsigned mismatches pass silently, checks are not thread-safe under tsan, and failures don't stop the test immediately.
Only one file (streams_tests.cpp) is converted so far as a proof of concept toward a full migration.

Code itself has been iterated on and is stable modulo IWYU nits; the open question is whether this design survives the competing Boost-removal effort.

categories.name: tests
why: P3 because it fixes a real but narrow class of hidden problems: Boost's check macros silently pass on signed/unsigned mismatches, break under tsan when used off the main thread, and confuse IWYU and clang-tidy tooling.

It improves CI signal quality (author cites a real CI log where the true failure was buried) but the PR only converts one file so far and a competing PR proposes removing Boost as the test runner entirely, which could supersede this approach.

result.summary: Adds a new set of thread-safe, fast-failing, overflow-safe test assertion macros (ASSERT, ASSERT_EQ, ASSERT_NE, ASSERT_LT/GT/LE/GE, ASSERT_EQ_COLLECTIONS, ASSERT_EXCEPTION) to src/test/util/common.h as a drop-in replacement for Boost's BOOST_CHECK family, and converts src/test/streams_tests.cpp to use them as a demonstration. The macros use std::source_location and C++20 concepts/ranges to produce readable failure messages and abort immediately on failure. Only one test file has been converted; the intent is to roll this out project-wide once accepted.
result.problem: Boost's check macros have several correctness and tooling problems that unit-test authors hit repeatedly: they compile and silently pass for mixed signed/unsigned comparisons (e.g. BOOST_CHECK_GT(-10, 10U) passes), they are not thread-safe and fail under tsan when called off the main thread, they cannot be reused in fuzz tests, they keep running after a failure making CI logs hard to read, and they confuse IWYU and clang-tidy. The author (a maintainer) says they keep running into these issues personally, including a case where CI logs did not show the real failure.

open_concerns: Whether losing Boost's continue-on-failure behavior (seeing all failing checks and full log context at once) is a net loss for debugging, raised by sedited; author proposed an opt-in env var as a compromise but has not implemented it.
How this PR relates to the parallel, more radical proposal (#35713) to remove Boost as the unit test runner entirely; author put this PR in draft partly for that reason.
resolved_concerns: sedited's initial skepticism about the value of fast-failing macros was addressed with concrete tsan/clang-tidy/IWYU evidence and a real CI log example, leading to a Concept ACK.
mercie-ux's nit about an unused <typeindex> include (later found to need adjustment per IWYU) was fixed in a subsequent push.

The author cites a concrete CI failure that was hidden in a 10000-line log because Boost kept running after the real failure. result.card: This PR adds new thread-safe, fast-failing, overflow-safe test assertion macros (ASSERT, ASSERT_EQ, ASSERT_EQ_COLLECTIONS, ASSERT_EXCEPTION) to replace Boost's BOOST_CHECK family in unit tests, converting one file (streams_tests.cpp) as a demonstration. It solves problems the author (a maintainer) says they repeatedly hit: Boost's macros silently pass on signed/unsigned mismatches, are not tsan-safe off the main thread, and hide real failures in long CI logs by continuing after the first failure. sedited raised a substantive objection about losing full-context debugging output but gave a Concept ACK after discussion; no unresolved objections remain. The author put the PR in draft because a conflicting PR (#35713) proposes removing Boost as the unit test runner entirely, which could make this incremental approach unnecessary, so review value depends on how that competing direction resolves.
